chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the fasting person who pours oil into his ear, he said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it

ai.seo_question: Does putting oil in the ear break the fast according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that instilling oil into the ear does not break the fast, a ruling derived from the principle that the ear is not a primary passage for nourishment like the mouth or nose. This establishes a key distinction in Shia fiqh between substances entering through the ears and those entering through the throat, affirming the validity of the fast despite the introduction of foreign matter.
